title-group.article-title: Analytical validation of a multiplex digital PCR assay for ESR1 mutations in advanced breast cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Great Lakes Cancer Consortium, Detroit, MI
Riverside University Medical Center, Chicago, IL

permissions.copyright-statement: © 2026 by American Society of Clinical Oncology

abstract.p: Background: Detection of ESR1 mutations is clinically relevant in advanced breast cancer, but routine testing can be limited by turnaround time, tissue availability, and workflow complexity. We developed and analytically validated a multiplex digital PCR assay for rapid molecular testing. Methods: The assay was designed to detect 12 clinically relevant ESR1 hotspot variants using plasma and formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue. Analytical sensitivity, specificity, precision, reproducibility, reportable range, and limit of detection were evaluated with reference materials, contrived specimens, and residual clinical samples. Testing used a minimum input of 8 ng. Orthogonal concordance was assessed against next-generation sequencing. Results: The assay achieved a limit of detection of 0.20% variant allele frequency. Overall analytical sensitivity was 98.5% and analytical specificity was 99.4%. Across 12 independent runs, the median coefficient of variation was 6.2%. Results were reproducible across operators, reagent lots, and instruments. Agreement with next-generation sequencing was 97.8%, with discordant samples concentrated near the analytical detection limit. Conclusions: This multiplex digital PCR assay provides sensitive, specific, and reproducible detection of ESR1 mutations in advanced breast cancer. The workflow may offer a practical alternative or complement to existing molecular methods when rapid results or limited specimen input are important. Prospective clinical validation is ongoing.
